content.value_statement: Data projects often lack clear rights, restrictions, and supporting evidence. This skill applies China's three-rights framework to produce structured findings and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Classifies data as self-generated, licensed, publicly collected, or purchased.
Screens for personal information, important data, intellectual property, trade secrets, and contract restrictions.
Maps data resource holding, processing and use, and data product operation rights.
Defines rights by dataset, purpose, territory, duration, transferability, and licensing scope.
Organizes source records, consent evidence, contracts, registrations, and authorization chains.
Drafts structured rights analyses, burden lists, remediation steps, and transaction frameworks.
limitations: It does not replace advice or formal opinions from licensed legal professionals.
Its framework primarily addresses Chinese data policy and law.
Conclusions depend on complete facts, contracts, consent records, and data inventories.
It cannot verify unseen evidence or predict regulator, court, auditor, or registry decisions.

use_cases.title: Assess data for accounting
use_cases.description: Review collection evidence, personal information constraints, and usable rights before a data resource accounting project.
use_cases.target_user: Corporate finance and data governance teams

use_cases.title: Review resale permissions
use_cases.description: Check a purchased dataset's contract, authorization chain, and operating rights before creating a commercial data product.

use_cases.title: Design rights governance
use_cases.description: Create a source inventory, rights register, evidence checklist, and internal controls for recurring data management.

prompt_templates.title: Classify one dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this dataset's source and identify the evidence needed to support lawful holding and use: [dataset and source].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single dataset

prompt_templates.title: Screen rights burdens
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [dataset] for personal information, important data, intellectual property, trade secrets, and contract restrictions. List missing facts and evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Map three rights
prompt_templates.prompt: Map holding, processing and use, and product operation rights for [parties and dataset]. Define scope, duration, territory, transfer, and licensing limits.

prompt_templates.title: Design a transaction structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [proposed data transaction]. Build an evidence matrix, identify authorization gaps, define a lawful rights flow, and propose contract protections and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: We collected customer behavior data and want to record it as an asset.
output_examples.output: Preliminary result: holding and use require lawful collection evidence. Separate personal information, verify consent and purpose limits, then document eligible derived resources.

output_examples.input: Our supplier contract allows internal analytics but says nothing about resale.
output_examples.output: The contract supports limited processing and use rights, not product operation or resale. Obtain explicit commercial and sublicensing rights before external distribution.

output_examples.input: Create a governance plan for sensor, partner, and public datasets.
output_examples.output: Create separate source records, burden checks, rights matrices, evidence folders, approval rules, and review dates for each dataset category.

best_practices: Provide dataset-level facts, parties, purposes, contracts, consent records, and intended transactions.
Separate legal collection, rights scope, and commercial feasibility into distinct conclusions.
Validate every conclusion against current law and qualified counsel before relying on it.
anti_patterns: Do not describe all data interests as ownership.
Do not infer resale rights from possession, payment, access, or internal-use permission.
Do not treat registration, anonymization, or processing as automatic proof of unrestricted rights.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a legal opinion?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured analysis and document planning for review by qualified legal professionals.

faq.question: Which legal framework does it use?
faq.answer: It focuses on China's data rights framework, including holding, processing and use, and data product operation rights.

faq.question: Can it decide whether purchased data may be resold?
faq.answer: It can review the stated contract terms and identify missing permissions. Final conclusions require the complete agreement and legal review.

faq.question: Does registration create data property rights?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats registration as evidence and public notice, not the original source of rights.

faq.question: Can personal information be treated as company property?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Personal information remains subject to personality rights and processing rules, regardless of company possession.

faq.question: What information produces the best analysis?
faq.answer: Provide data inventories, collection methods, contracts, consent records, processing purposes, parties, territories, durations, and planned uses.
